About the Conference
                        Libraries for Tomorrow Conference 2026 brings together library professionals to explore how rapid technological change is reshaping the future of knowledge and access. Under the theme The Future is Now: Adapting to Exponential Change, we go beyond the library’s walls to examine shifts in our social fabric, explore how information is being created and consumed, and consider the technological possibilities on the horizon. Expect panel discussions and poster presentations that showcase how libraries are not just responding to change, but are leading it in their own communities. Join us in reaffirming the library’s enduring role as a democratic space for learning, opportunity, and connection.

Poster Competition
                                                    Competition Details                                                
                                                    Got a bold idea or innovative project to share? We invite poster submissions that showcase how libraries are adapting to rapid changes—through transformative ways of working, creative uses of technology, or new approaches to professional practice.
For this exciting event, stand to win these top cash prizes:
 First Place: $1,000
 Second Place: $500
 Third Place: $250
Posters should highlight projects and/or initiatives undertaken by your libraries, or ideas in any of the following sub-themes:
                                                    Sub-Themes: (1) Future of Libraries                                                
                                                    This theme explores how libraries are adapting to rapidly evolving user needs, emerging trends and shifting expectations.
Submissions may highlight projects or initiatives to do with:
 Community engagement and impact
 Environmental sustainability in library operations, collections, and services
 Inclusivity and accessibility
Partnerships and collaborations
                                                    Sub-Themes: (2) Future of Technology                                                
                                                    This theme explores how technology is shaping the future of libraries.
Submissions may:
 Highlight how emerging technologies (e.g. AI, immersive experiences, etc.) or existing technologies have been applied to libraries in new and impactful ways.
 Share implementation insights, including challenges, risks, and lessons learned.
 Address ethics and governance issues around technology, including responsible use guidelines and policies.
 Share best practices in user education, for example, how libraries are supporting users in an ever-changing information landscape.
                                                    Sub-Themes: (3) Future of Librarianship                                                
                                                    This theme explores how librarianship is evolving.
Submissions may showcase:
Case studies of evolving roles
 Case studies of a library professional of the future (e.g. Future roles, skills, or work environment), supported by relevant trends or insights where possible
 Case studies of new ways of working (e.g. Introduction of agile teams, cross-discipline partnerships)
 Skills development and training initiatives (e.g. AI literacy workshops, professional development pathways)
                                                    Submission Guidelines                                                
                                                    📅 Deadline: 23 September 2026 (Wed)
📝Poster Submission:
 All posters must be submitted in A1 size (594 x 841 mm) and PDF format.
 Please also submit:
 500-word description explaining your poster’s concept and message.
 150-word bio highlighting your name, affiliations and expertise.
Selected participants will be notified and kindly requested to arrange printing of their posters (A1 size) for showcase at LAS Conference 2026.
Stay tuned! Winners of the Poster Competition will be announced at the conference.
                                                    Evaluation Criteria                                                
                                                    1) Relevance to Theme
 Alignment with Conference Theme: How well does the poster address the conference’s overarching theme of how libraries can adapt to rapid change?
Significance to Libraries: Is the topic timely and relevant to current trends and challenges in the library field?
2) Project Description and Impact
Project Goals and Objectives: Are the goals and objectives of the project clearly stated and well-defined?
 Evidence of Impact: Does the submission demonstrate clear or plausible impact on the library or community, supported by metrics, feedback, outcomes, or relevant trends and insights?
3) Innovation and Creativity
Originality: Does the poster present original ideas in the specified areas?
Novelty of Approach and Creativity: Does the project offer an innovative or unique approach to solving a problem or addressing a need? Is the solution creative and forward-thinking?
4) Visual Appeal and Presentation
Aesthetics & Clarity of Visuals: Are the visuals appealing, clear, relevant, and well-organised to support the poster’s message?
Balance of Text and Graphics: Is there a good balance between text and graphics, ensuring that both elements complement each other?
5) Educational Value
Teaching and Learning Opportunities: Does the project offer valuable lessons or insights that can be shared with other libraries or professionals?
Best Practices and Educational Impact: Does the project contribute to the development or dissemination of best practices in the library field? Is there potential for the project’s findings or methods to be used in educational settings or professional development?
Questions?
Please send your enquiries to conference@las.org.sg
Call for Papers
We look forward to your participation and would like to invite you to submit papers for the following themes:
                                        (1) Future of Libraries                                    
                                        (2) Future of Technology                                    
                                        (3) Future of Librarianship                                    
                                        Submission Guidelines                                    
                                            This theme explores how libraries are adapting to rapidly evolving user needs, emerging trends and shifting expectations.
How do libraries support sustainability and the environment in the digital age?
How do library patrons view libraries, and how would they like libraries to meet their information needs?
Evolving library functions and purposes e.g. the role of libraries in supporting mental health
                                            This theme explores how technology is shaping the future of libraries.
 Submissions may include:
How libraries balance the human element (staff and users) while embracing technology for more engaging experiences
Redefining possibilities amidst technical issues and funding challenges
Case studies on the use of technology in libraries
                                            This theme explores how librarianship is evolving.
 Submissions may investigate:
New roles for librarians
Relationships between users and librarians
Training for future librarians

                Conference Speakers
Opening Keynote Speaker
Warren Fernandez
Warren Fernandez is Senior Fellow and Head of the National Security Studies Programme at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies (RSIS), Nanyang Technological University (NTU), and Editor of RSIS Publications. He also serves as Senior Advisor at NTU’s Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information (WKWSCI).
A former Editor of The Straits Times and CEO of Edelman Asia Pacific, he has over three decades of leadership experience in media and communications. He contributes to public service through roles that include Board Member of the National Arts Council and National Library Board, and Member of Singapore’s Public Service Commission. Warren holds degrees from Oxford University and Harvard University’s John F. Kennedy School of Government.
Future of Libraries Panellist
Assoc Prof Loh Chin Ee
National Institute of Education
Loh Chin Ee is Associate Professor at the English Language and Literature Department and Associate Dean (Impact and Partnerships) at the Office for Research at the National Institute of Education, Nanyang Technological University. Her research focuses on young people’s reading at the intersection of globalisation and technological changes as well as the role of school libraries in fostering reading for pleasure and lifelong learning. Her most recent books are The Reading Lives of Teens: Research & Practice (Routledge, 2025, UKLA Academic Book Award) and Little Things: An Anthology of Poetry (2nd Edition, Ethos, 2025).
Future of Libraries Panellist
Ng Kah Gay
Ethos Books & Pagesetters
As publisher, Kah Gay focuses on making books and supporting an environment for literature, the arts and culture in Singapore and Southeast Asia. The passionate and experienced team is part of a growing ecology of independent agents producing and circulating fiction, non-fiction and poetry that speak to our times, including critical concerns such as climate action.
Future of Libraries Panellist
Sarah Mineko Ichioka
Desire Lines
Sarah Ichioka leads and advises places, communities, and organizations to chart paths toward thriving futures. Her work has explored the intersections of cities, society and ecology with and for prominent institutions of policy, culture and research across four continents. A board steward, author and public speaker, she has been recognised as an Honorary Fellow of the Royal Institute of British Architects, Designing Cities for All Fellow of Pakhuis de Zwijger (Netherlands), and Treseder Fellow of the Melbourne School of Design (Australia).
Lecture Speaker
Asst Prof Setsuko Yokoyama
Singapore University of Technology and Design
Setsuko Yokoyama is Assistant Professor of Digital Humanities at Singapore University of Technology and Design. Trained as a literary historian, her work concerns the sociopolitical history of speech-to-text technology in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, and its implications for our contemporary discourse on fairness in automated speech recognition systems.
Future of Technology Panellist
Lim Bee Kwan
Assurity Trusted Solutions and Singapore Computer Society
With over 30 years of experience in Infocomm Technology, Bee Kwan is CEO of Assurity Trusted Solutions and has previously held senior leadership positions in various public sector organizations including cybersecurity and digital governance, as well as headed the Government Infrastructure, overseeing the entire spectrum of ICT systems for public sector.
Future of Technology Panellist
Dr Ngui Jian Gang
AI Singapore
Jian Gang is the Head of Model Development in AI Singapore, and leads the team that develops the SEA-LION family of models, including safety models and embedding models, as well as the team that develops the SEA-HELM evaluation suite and maintains the SEA-HELM leaderboard. He and his team also has formalised their work into various research publications, including ‘SEA-LION: Southeast Asian Languages in One Network’, ‘SEA-HELM: Southeast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models’, ‘SEA-Guard: Culturally Grounded Multilingual Safeguard for Southeast Asia’, ‘SEA-SafeguardBench: Evaluating AI Safety in SEA Languages and Cultures’, and ‘SEA-BED: Southeast Asia Embedding Benchmark’.
Future of Technology Panellist
Dr Natalia Grincheva
LASALLE, University of the Arts Singapore
Dr Grincheva is 2026 Digital Statecraft Academic Cambridge Fellow and a leading Digital Humanities scholar and practitioner who specializes in data-driven cultural policy and diplomacy. Her work actively shapes the emerging field of digital statecraft, bridging the gap between cultural insight and data-driven governance. Her career spans from foundational work on the UNESCO’s 2005 Convention to pioneering the Data To Power platform. Her publications include three monographs Geopolitics of Digital Heritage (Cambridge University Press: 2024), Museum Diplomacy in the Digital Age (Routledge: 2020) and Global Trends in Museum Diplomacy (Routledge: 2019).
Future of Librarianship Panellist
Aaron Tay
Singapore Management University
Aaron Tay is Head of Data Services at Singapore Management University Libraries, with over 15 years of experience in academic librarianship. His work spans research support, open access, analytics, bibliometrics, discovery systems, and emerging technologies. He is the author of Musings about Librarianship, a long-running blog where he reflects on librarianship issues, with a recent focus on AI-powered academic search tools. Aaron is especially interested in how libraries are responding to current AI trends, including how librarians can critically evaluate AI and data-intensive tools, separate genuine value from hype, and support researchers in using them responsibly.
Future of Librarianship Panellist
Koh Chern Chern
Singapore Polytechnic
Chern Chern has more than 2 decades of experience across academic library functions. She has held leadership roles spanning cataloguing, projects, user services, outreach and operations, driving transformation initiatives including self-service library innovations.
Her current work focuses on library automation, records management and integrating AI-enabled resources and services to support curriculum design and higher-order learning outcomes. She is passionate about advancing libraries as strategic partners in applied education, digital transformation, and lifelong learning.
Future of Librarianship Panellist
Gee Miaw Miin
National Library Board
Miaw Miin began her career as a librarian with the Geylang East Branch Library and has since immersed herself in more than three decades of practice spanning public libraries, reference services, media literacy instruction, and career development of library and archives professionals. She has played a key role in the development and implementation of NLB’s library & archives competency framework, specialist career framework, and specialist career development pathways. She also serves on the project team developing and implementing the Library Association of Singapore’s Competency Framework for Information Professionals. Miaw Miin believes in building a future-ready library profession through purposeful career pathways and competency-driven development.
